title: Drops for a Wriggly Child

patient.name: Baby Nurul (with mother)
patient.presenting_complaint: Charted eye drops for a young child; mother needs to learn how to instil them at home

history.hpc: The mother says 'My girl keep struggling and crying, I scared to put the drop wrongly.' The child is prescribed drops and the mother needs to be taught a safe technique for a wriggly young child at home.
history.pmhx: Young child, otherwise well. No known drug allergies (confirm with parent).
history.allergies: No drug allergy recorded on file.
history.social_hx: Cared for by her mother at home.

va.right: Not the focus of this station
va.left: Not the focus of this station

examination_findings.anterior_segment: No active infection that would change technique

investigations.task: Instil the drop safely in a young child and teach the parent a practical home technique
investigations.key_points: Confirm identity and allergy with the parent; lay the child down or gently wrap if needed; pull the lower lid and place a drop in the inner corner / lower pocket; if the child squeezes, the drop in the corner runs in when the eye opens; never force or touch the eye with the tip

diagnosis: The drop is instilled safely in a young child and the parent is taught a practical home technique: laying the child down, placing a drop in the inner corner / lower lid pocket, and letting it run in when the eye opens, without forcing the eye or touching the tip. Identity and allergy are confirmed with the parent. This is a procedural/teaching station.

immediate: Confirm the child's identity and check allergy with the parent
Confirm the correct eye and the charted drop and strength
Position the child lying down, gently steadied/wrapped if needed, with the parent assisting
Pull the lower lid and place one drop in the inner corner / lower pocket without touching the eye or tip
If the child squeezes the eye shut, the drop in the corner runs in when the eye opens
Reassure and comfort the child afterwards
Document the drop, eye, time and allergy check, and teach the parent
follow_up: Confirm the parent feels able to do the drops at home
Advise returning if the eye worsens or the child cannot tolerate the drops
patient_education: Teach the parent the lying-down, inner-corner technique
Reassure that a drop in the corner still works when the eye opens
Advise never to force the eye or touch the bottle tip to the eye

key_points: Confirms the child's identity and the charted drop with the parent
Explains the plan to the parent
Engages calmly with the child and parent
Positions the child safely (lying down, gently steadied)
Places a drop in the inner corner / lower pocket with a no-touch technique
Does not force the eye open
Confirms the drop reaches the eye when it opens
Recognises the challenge of drops in a young child
Knows the inner-corner technique for an uncooperative child
Teaches the parent a practical home technique
Documents the drop, eye, time and allergy check
Comforts the child and reassures the parent
